DELHI ADMINISTRATION, 

DELHI 

NOTIFICATION 

No. F.l 3(76)/ 61 Press. 2nd December 1961. 
Whereas it appears to the Chief Commissioner, 
Delhi, that the booklet entitled “A Study in the 
Ethics of the Banishment of Sita”, written in 
English, published by “Santa” Magazine, New 
Delhi, and printed at the Delhi Press, New Delhi, 
contains matter, which is deliberately and 

maliciously intended to outrage the religious feel- 
ings of a class of the citizens of India, viz., Hindus 
who regard “Ram” as Autar, by insulting the 
religion or the religious beliefs ol that class, that is 
to say, the matter, the publication of which is 
punishable under section 295A of the Indian Penal 
Code Act (XLV of I860); 

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers con- 
ferred bv section 99A of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure (Act V of 1898), the Chief Commissioner, 
Delhi, hereby declares to be forfeited to Govern- 
ment every copy of the said booklet and all othei 
documents containing copies, reprints and transla- 
tions of or extracts Irom the said book. 

Bv order, 

K. M. L. GUPTA, 
Under Scev. (Home).

(1) Instructions regarding submission of application.—

the blanks are filled up in the candidates’ own handwriting. 

( 2 ) Particulars and certificates required.— Candidates 

should furnish evidence of their age, qualifications and 
previous experience together with certificates written not 
more than one year prior to the date of their applications, 
trom responsible persons, testilying to their private 
character. 

The Commission accepts only the age of a candidate as 
lecorded in the Matriculation or the Secondary School 
Final/ Leaving (Certificate. In the case of a female candi- 
date wnose age is not recorded in the Matriculation or 
School Final Certificate, any of the following evidence ot 
ago is accepted by the Commission: — 

1. A certificate from the Headmistress of the school 

which she last attended, showing her exact age as 
recorded in the scfiool register. 

2. An affidavit regarding her age sworn by her father 

or mother or some other person in a position to 
know by having been present or heard of her birth 
at the time of occurrence. 

8. A certificate regarding her age, from a Member of 
the Legislature or a gazetted officer, who must 
have known the candidate and her family, indicat- 
ing clearly the evidence on the basis oi which he/ 
she satisfied him self/ herself on the point. 

(A) Fee.- Candidates must enclose with fheir apolica- 
tions a fee of H«. 5 in the form of a receipted clialan 
from a Government Treason or the Reserve Bank of india 
under i ho head “XXXV 1 — Miscellaneous — Receipts of the 
1'ublie Service Commission, West Bengal”. Money <,rden», 
cheques, etc., in lieu of treasury ehallans are not accepted 
Postal order, however, may be accepted from candidates. 
Thej should he crossed and made payable to “The Secre- 
tary, Public Service Commission, West Bengal”. No appli- 
cation will be considered unless accompanied with the 
requisite application fee. 

Candidates abroad may deposit their application fees 
with the High Commissioner of India or the Embassy, as 
the case may he, and obtain receipts for the same, which 
will have to he at, Lathed to their applications to be sub- 
mitted to the Commission, 

Candidates in Co\ eminent service should make *ure

(ii) A member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled

(4) Address. — Candidates should give their present

change of address. 

(5) Canvassing. — Any attempt on the jmrt of candidates 
to enlist support of their applications through persons of 
lullnence or officials of Government will disqualify them 
tor appointment. Spontaneous recommendation from 
jiorsons interested in the candidates or otherwise known 
to them will he disregarded. 

(6) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under ary Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Damodar Valley Corporation), in 
India will ho rejected unless they are submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service. 

Candidates serving under Government or a local or 
Statutory Body should submit an advance copy in the pres- 
cribed form. The application fee should in such cases be 
attached to the advance copy and not to the original. The 
candidature of such applicants may not however be con- 
sidered if the original applications do not reach the Com- 
mission’s office within a fortnight from the (dosing date. 
Unless applications in original or advance copies with 
application fees are received within the closing date, late 
applications may he rejected.

Scheme No. LXXV1 (Broad Street to Palm Avenue 
— Tiljala Lane) 

CORRIGENDUM 

In the notice under section 43 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act, 1911 (Bengal Act V of 1911), in 
regard to Scheme No. LXXVI (Broad Street to 
Palm Avenue — Tiljala Lane), published in the Supple- 
ment to the “Calcutta Gazette”, dated the 28th Sep- 
tember, 5th October and 12th October 1961, on pages 
779-780. 787-789 and 827-828 respectively— 

Add premises No. *17/1/1’ after ‘17/1’ and before 
‘17/2’ under “Broad Street” in the “List of 
municipal premises proposed to be acquired”. 

K. SEN, Chairman. 

!() Netaji Subhas Road, 

Calcutta-1, 

Dated 3rd January 1962. 


The Board of Trustees for the Improvement of 
Calcutta 

NOTICE UNDER SECTION 43 OF THE 
CALCUTTA IMPROVEMENT ACT, 1911 
(BENGAL ACT V OF 1911) 

Scheme No. LXXX1 (Muraripukur Road) 

Dated Calcutta, the 16th December 1961. 

1. It is hereby notified under section 43 of the 
Calcutta Improvement Act, that an improvement 
sJieme, namely, Scheme No. LXXXI (Muraripukur 
[Road) for the purpose of rehousing bustee dwellers, 
providing building sites, remedying defective ventila- 
tion, creating new or improving existing means of 
communication and facilities for traffic and afford- 
ing better facilities for conservancy, has been framed 
pv the Board of Trustees for the Improvement of 
Calcutta in an area within Constituency No. 15 of 
the Corporation of Calcutta. 


' - The area comprised within and affected by the 
cheme shown within red verge on the plan has the 
following boundaries: — 

On the North: Starting from a point on the 
eastern boundary of 20 Canal East Road about 
6 ft. 0 inch, on the south from its north- 
eastern corner eastward along the southern 
boundary of No. 18, Canal East Road to its 
south-eastern corner, then eastward north- 
ward and again eastward along the southern, 
eastern and southern boundary of No. 15/ 1C, 
Muraripukur Road to a point on the western 
edge of Muraripukur Road, then eastward in 
a straight line for a distance of 118 ft. across 


Muraripukur Road and Premises No. 35G, 
Muraripukur Road to a point about 137 ft. 
from the south-western corner of 35G Murari- 
pukur Road. 

On the East: From this point southward in a 
straight line for a distance of 532 ft. across 
premises No. 35G, Muraripukur Road, C. C. 
Road and drain, premises Nos. 41 B, 41 C and 
41 D. Muraripukur Road to a point about 
103 ft. from the south-eastern corner of No. 13, 
Muraripukur Road.

Sr 1 tion i. — Purposes of Article . 

To enable the Association to fulfil the functions with 
which it is entrusted, the status, immunities mid privileges 
provided in this Article shall be accorded to the -Association 
in the territories of each member. 

Section 2.— Status of the Association . 

The Association shall possess full juridical personality 
and, in particular, the capacity: 

( /) to contract ; 

(it) to inquire and dispose of immovable and movable 
property ; 

iiii) to institute* legal proceedings. 

Section d. — Position of the Association with regard to 


Judicial Process. 

Actions may be brought against the Association only in 
courl of competent jurisdiction in the territories of a member 
in which tin* Association lias nn office, has appointed an 
agent for the purpose of accepting service or notice* of 
process, or has issued or guaranteed securities. No actions 
shall, however, be brought by members or persons acting 
tor ot deriving claims from members. The property and 
assets of tin* Association shall, wheresoever located and by 
whomsoever litdd, be immune from alt forms of seizure, 
attachment or execution before the delivery of final judgment 
against the Association. 


Section 4 . — Immunity of Assets from Seizure. 

Property and assets of the Association, wherever located 
and by whomsoever held, shall be immune from search, 
requisition, confiscation, expropriation or any other form of 
seizure by executive or legislative action. 


Section 5 . — Immunity <>4 Archives. 

The archives of the Association shall be inviolable.

of this Agreement, all property and assets of the Association 
shall be free from restrictions, regulations, controls and 
morntoria of any nature.

Tin 1 official communications of the Associations shall be 
accorded by each member the same treatment that it accords

immunity ;

m) shall be granted the same treatment in respect of

comparable rank of other members. 

Section f ). — 1 mm unities from Ta.ral ion . 

i a ) The Association, its assets, property, income and 
transactions authorized by this Agreement, shall he immune 
from nil taxation and from all customs duties. The 
Association shall also be immune from liability for the

PART II — Advertisements, Notices 

Procedure regarding tending Manuscripts for publication of Advertisements, Notices, oto., in the 

“Caloutta Gazette” (Part II). 

1. Manuscripts should be properly edited and complete in itself. 

2. Manuscripts should always be typewritten on one side of the paper. The name of signatory should be typewritten 
below the signature. 

3. Manuscripts intended for advertisement in the next issue of “Calcutta Gazette" shall be received by Publication Sales 
Office of New Secretariat Buildings, 1 Hastings Street, Calcutta, up to 3-30 p. m. on Friday and at Head Office at Alipore up to 
11 a. m. on Saturday. 

4. All costs shall be paid in advance and deposited along with the manuscripts. 

5. Manuscripts and postal remittances shall be addressed to SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT PRINTING (PUBLICATION 
BRANCH), WE8T BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRESS, ALIPORE. 

The press shall not be held responsible for delay in publication of any advertisement due to the non-ooservance of tb s 
Instructions deiaHed above. ~

(Appointment by Competitive Examination) Regula- 
tions, 1955, namely:— 

1. These regulations may be called the Indian 
Administrative Service (Appointment by Competitive 
Examination) Amendment Regulations, 1961.

ment by Competitive Examination) Regulations 1955, 
— below sub-regulation (i) of Regulation 4, insert the 
following proviso: 

“Provided that until the State of Pondicherry 
becomes part of India, a person born or 
resident in that State in whose favour a 
certificate of eligibility has been issued by the 
Government of India shall also be eligible to 
compete at the examination.”

GOVERNMENT OF BIHAR 
Political (Special) Department 
NOTIFICATION 
Patna, the 30th January 1962. 

No. A/Prs. Ste.-102/62-l 139C. — Whereas it 
appears to the Governor of Bihar that the booklet in 
Hindi entitled “Isai Dharma Granth Bible”, written 
by Shri Harish Chandra Vidhyarthi, published by 
All India Dayanand Salvation Mission, Hoshiarpur, 
and printed at Saboo Press, Ranchi, contains dis- 
paraging remarks against Jesus Christ, Virgin Mary 
and the Bible, which are deliberately and maliciously 
intended to outrage the religious feelings of the 
Christians by insulting their religious beliefs and 
which are intended to promote feelings of enmity and 
hatred between the Christians and Hindus; 

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred 
bv section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 
1898, the Governor is pleased to declare the said 
booklet, and every copy of the booklet, all extracts 
therefrom and all other documents containing copies, 
reprints or translations thereof, to be forfeited to 
Government. 

* 

By order of the Governor, 

B. M. P. S1NHA, Under Secy.

CORPORATION OF CALCUTTA 

NOTICE 

Dated the 2nd March 1962 

NOTICE is hereby given for the information of the 
public that the Corporation of Calcutta under powers 
vested unto it, has by its resolution, dated the 29th 
December 1961, prescribed the alignments of two 
30 ft. projected streets, i.e., (a) one running north to 
South connecting Fern Road with a 30 ft. road con- 
structed by Hindusthan Corporation Insurance 
Society Ltd. (now Ekdalia Place) and (b) the other 
running east to west connecting Ballygunge Station 
Road with aforesaid 30 ft. road under section 356 
read with section 363 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 
1951, as shown in the plan prepared for the purpose 
in Ward No. 61 (old No. 27). 

A copy of plan prepared in this behalf may be 
seen in the office of the Chief Valuer and Surveyor on 
any working day during the hours of 11 a.m. and 
2 p.m. on payment of usual fees. 

P. C. MAJUMDAR, Commissioner.

DELHi ADMIN. STRATI ON, DEI Hi 
NOTIFICATION 

No. F-37/62-C. — 22nd February 1962.— 

vVhcreas the Chief Commissioner, Delhi, is 
satisfied that the book without title in Urdu 
published by Saeed, House No. 1368, Gali Zakirya, 
Phatak Habash Khan, Delhi, and printed at Khanna 
Litho Press, Delhi, contains matters which is deli- 
berately and maliciously intended to outrage the reli- 
g.ous feelings of the Muslims of India by insulting 
their religious beliefs and the publication of which is 
punishable under section 295 A of the Indian Penal 
Code (Act XLV of 1860); 

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred 
bv section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 
i 898 (Act V of 1898), the Chief Commissioner, Delhi, 
hereby declares to be forfeited to Government eve 

T'v of the said book and all other documents con- 
ainmg copies, reprints and translations of or extracts 
from the said book. 

By order, 

K.M. L. GUPTA. Under Secy. (Home). 


GOVERNMENT OF BIHAR 
Political (Special) Department 
NOTIFICATION 
Patna, the 15th February 1962. 

No. A/Prs.Ste-101 /62-C-1796-C. — Whereas, it 
Wears to the Governor of Bihar that the book in 
Hindi, entitled “Chin-Ki-Jhalak“ published from 
foreign Language Publications, Peking 1958, con- 
tains two maps on the inner cover of the book 
Wnch wrongly show practically the whole of 
rifFA, and portions of Jammu and Kashmir, 
Himachal Pradesh, U.P. and Bhutan, as part of 


China, which amounts to questioning the territorial 
integrity or frontiers of India in a manner which 
is likely to be prejudicial to the interests oj the 
safety or security of India, the publication oi whiJi 
is punishable under section 2 of the Criminal Law 
Amendment Act, 1961 (Central Act 23 of 1961); 

Now, therefore, in exercise ol the powers con- 
ferred by sub-section (1) of section 4 ol the said 
Act, the Governor of Bihar hereby declares every 
copy of the aforesaid book and all other documents 
containing copies, reprints or translation of or 
extracts from the said book to be forfeited to the 
Government. 

By order of the Governor of Bihar, 
M. SINHA, Dy. Sec>

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 

BENGAL ENGINEERING COLLEGE 

P.O. Botanic Garden, Howrah 

THE Bengal Engineering College will open next 
session on july 2, 1962. The College is a residential 
one and otters courses tor the B.E. Degree Examina- 
tion ot the Calcutta University m Civil, Mechanical, 
Electrical, Metallurgical, Mining t ,nu ) ele-^ommuai- 
cation Engineering and also foi the Degree in 
Aiehitecture. Admission will be granted on the 
results ot an admission test consisting of a written 
examination for all candidates to be conducted by 
the ‘'West Bengal Board of Examination or Admis- 
sion to Engineering Colleges" as per dates given 
below which will be followed by a medical tisi and 
viva-voce test. Applications must be made in ttm 
prescribed form with a crossed Indian Postal Order 
showing deposit ol Rs. 12 ;Rs. 6 being the registra- 
tion fee payable to the Board plus Rs. 6 payable to 
each College to which admission is sought) payable 
to the “West Bengal Boaid of Examination for admis- 
sion to Engineering Colleges” and should each t!m 
Office of the Board, c/o Bengal Engineering College. 
PO. Botanic Garden, Howrah, on or belore April 
18, 1962. The College prospectus and requisite 
application forms may be obtained from the college 
°flice either personally or by sending an unstamped 
self-addressed envelope of 10"x4$" size on and 
from 26th March 1962. A number of scholarships 
and stipends will be awarded to meritorious 
students, on the results of the Admission Test. 
Applications for the Five-year integrated degree 
course under the new regulations of the Calcutta 
University will be entertained from candidates v»ho 
nave either passed or will appear this year in the 


Pie- University Examination of the Calcutta Uni- 
versity or the Higher Secondary Examination in the 
Science stream or the Technical stream of the 
Board ol Secondary Education, West Bengal, with 
Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics or its equi- 
valent. The selection of the candidates who have 
appeared in either of these qualifying examinations* 
will however be subject to their passing these exami- 
nations this year. Candidates must not be over 
19 years of age on January 1, 1962. The age limit 
may be relaxed up to 21 years with the prior appro- 
val of the Government in the case of deserving 
applicants belonging to the educationally backward 
classes and communities. Further details regarding 
admission, number of seats in different branches, 
examination syllabus, programme, etc. are given in 
the prospectus. 

Dates of Admission Test

dates). 

3 p.m. to 5 p.m. — English Composition and Precis 
Writing (for all candidates).

10 a.m. to 12 noon- -Physics (for all candidates). 
12-30 p.m. to 2-30 p.m. — Chemistry (for all 
candidates). 

Wednesday, May 23, 1962 — 

10 a.m. to 1 p.m. — Free hand Drawing (Archi 
tecture candidates only).

General instructions to candidates applying In response te

{ [) instructions regarding submission of application. - 

Applications are to be made on the prescribed form which

typed (not handwritten) form showing exactly the word- 
ing {Mid spacing of the sample form published in the

the blanks are filled up in the candidates’ own handwriting. 

U) particulars and certificates required.— Candidates 

should furnish evidence of their age, qualifications and 
previous experience together with certificates written not 
more than one .year prior to the date of their applications, 
irom responsible persons, testifying to their private 
character. 

The Commission accepts only the age of a candidate as 
i .Horded in the Matriculation or the Secondary School 
Final /heaving Certificate. In the case of a female candi- 
date wnose age is not recorded in the Matriculation or 
School Final Certificate, any of the following evidence of’ 
ai:t* s accepted by the Commission: — 

1. A certificate from the Headmistress of the school 

which she last attended, showing her exact age an 
recorded in the school register. 

2. An affidavit regarding her age sworn by her father 

or mother or some other person in a position to 
know by having been present or heard of her birth 
at the time of occurrence. 

A certificate regarding her age, from a Member of 
the Legislature or a gazetted officer, who must 
have known the candidate and her family, indicat- 
ing clearly the evidence on the basis of which he/ 
she satisfied himself /herself on the point. 

U) Fee.— Candidates must enclose with their applica- 
tions a fee of Re. 6 in the form of a receipted cfialan 
from a Government Treasury or the Reserve Bank of India 
the head “XXXVI — Miscellaneous — Receipts of the 
i unlio Service Commission, West Bengal”. Money erden*, 
J'^ues, etc., in lieu of treasury challans are not accepted 
o*»tal order, however, may he accepted from candidates. 

, - ? should be crossed and made payable to “The Secre- 
lfi ry, Public Service Commission, West Bengal”. No appli- 
will be considered unless accompanied with the 
requisite application fee. 

^didates abroad may deposit their application fees 
tn the High Commissioner of India or the Embassy, as 
win < u W0 may be > and obtain receipts for the same, which 
, ni4i j av ® to be attached to their applications to he sub-

with^u ,r 8 1 ,, P er *°r officers. In no case will the fee paid

The Commission may remit fee in case of genuinely 
indigent and bona fide displaced person from Pakistan. 

An indigent displaced person shall, in the first instance, 
pay the application fee prescribed tor a gazetted poet 
advertised by the Commission but if he /she is selected for 
and appears at the interview, the fee paid by him/her will 
be refunded afterwards. 

Note. — “(i) A uisplaeed porson claiming age concession 
must furnish with his application satisfactory evidence 
that he is bona fide displaced person from Pakistan, e.g 
refugee registration card or a certificate from a gazetted 
officer or a Member of Parliament or State Legislature, in 
original. 

(ii) A member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled 
Tribe claiming age concession must furnish with bis appli- 
ratum a certificate in original from a gazetted officer or a 
Member of Parliament or State Legislature belonging to 
the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, specifying the 
particular caste or tribe to which he claims to belong. 

(m) A displaced person seeking remission of the applica- 
tion lee must furnish besides the evidence required under 
Note ( 1 ) above, a certificate (in original) from a District 
Officer or a gazetted officer or a Member of Parliament or 
State Legislature to show that he is not in a position to 
pay the prescribed fee.” 

(4) Address. — Candidates should give their preeent 
address and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of address 

(6) Canvassing. — Any attempt on the part of candidates 
to enlist support of their applications through persons of 
influence or officials of Government will disqualify them 
tor appointment. Spontaneous recommendation from 
IKirsons interested in the candidates or otherwise known 
to them will he disregarded. 

(6) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under any Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Damodar Valley Corporation), in 
India will he rejected unless they are submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service. 

Candidates serving under Government or a local or 
Statutory Body should submit an advance copy in the pres- 
cribed form. The application fee should in such cases be 
attached to the advance copy and not to the original. The 
candidature of such applicants may not however be con- 
sidered if the original applications do not reach the Com- 
mission’s office within a fortnight from the closing date. 
Unless applications in original or advance copies with 
application fees are received within the closing date, late 
applications may be rejected.

from the State oi West Bongol to the State of Maha- 
rastra, and accordingly, the words ‘State ol Maha- 
rastra” he substituted for the words State ol West 
llengal”, in Clause II of the Memorandum of Asso- 
ciation of the Company”.

Benerai instructions to candidates applying In response to 
advertisements issued by the Commission for reorult- 
ment to posts of “ Selection". 

(l) Instructions regarding submission of application. - 

Applications are to be made on the prescribed form which 
ffl ll he available from the office of the Public Service Com- 
mission, West Bengal, Anderson House (ground floor), 
Alipore, Calcuua-27, personally or on sending a large self- 
uidressed envelope with stamps sufficient to cover the 
Wage affixed to it. Candidates who are unable to obtain 

copies of the prescribed form may apply on any similar 
typed (not handwritten) form showing exactly the word- 
wd spacing of the sample form published in the 
Calcutta Gazette” of the let September 1955, provided 
the blanks are filled up in the candidates’ own handwriting. 


Co mmis s io n accepts only the age of a candidate as 
recorded in the Matriculation or the Secondary School 
Final /Leaving Certificate. In the case of a female candi- 
date whose asm u not recorded in the Matriculation or 
School Final Certificate, any of the following evidence oft 
age *s accepted by the Commission: — 

1. A certificate from the Headmistress of the school 

which she last attended, showing her exact age as 
recorded in the school register. 

2. An affidavit regarding her age sworn by her father 

or mother or some other person in a position to 
know by having been present or heard of her birth 
at the time of occurrence. 

H. A certificate regarding her age, from a Member of 
the Legislature or a gazetted officer, who must, 
have known the candidate and her family, indicat- 
ing clearly the evidence on the basis of which he/ 
she satisfied himself/ herself on the point. 

(3) Fee.- Candidates must enclose with their apolica- 
tions a fee of Re. 5 In the form of a receipted ohatan 
from a Government Treasury or the Reserve Bank of India 
under the head “XXXVI — Miscellaneous — Receipts of the 
Puhlic Service Commission, West Bengal”. Money order*, 
cheques, etc., in lieu of treasury challans are not accepted 
Postal order, however, may be accepted from candidates. 
They should be crossed and made payable to “The Secre- 
tary, Public Service Commission, West Bengal”. No appli- 
cation will be considered unless accompanied with the 
requisite application fee. 

Candidates abroad may deposit their application fees 
with the High Commissioner of India or the Embasey, as 
tb* <*** may he, and obtain receipts for the same, which 
wi» have to be attached to their applications to be sub- 
mitted to the Commission. 

Candidates in Government service should make «ure 
before depositing fee that their applications will be forward- 
ed by their superior officers. In no case will the fee paid 
with the application be refunded. 

The Commission may remit fee in case of genuinely 
indigent and bona fide displaced person from Pakistan. 

An indigent displaced person shall, in the first instance, 
pay ; the application fee prescribed for a gazetted poet 
advertised by the Commission but if he/she is selected for 
and appears at the interview, the fee paid by him/her will 
be refunded afterwards. 

Note. — “(i) A displaced person claiming age concession 
must furnish with his application satisfactory evidence 
that he is bona fide displaced person from Pakistan, e.g 
refugee registration card or a certificate from a gazetted 
officer or a Member of Parliament or State Legislature in 
original. * 

(ii) A member of the Scheduled Caste or Soheduled 
Tribe claiming age concession must furnish with his appli- 
cation a certificate in original from a gazetted officer or a 
Member of Parliament or State Legislature belonging to 
the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, specifying the 
particular caste or tribe to which he claims to belong. 


(iii) A displaced person seeking remission of the applica- 
tion tee must furnish besides the evidence required under 
Note (i) above, a certificate (in original) from a District 
Officer or a gazetted officer or a Member of Parliament or 
State Legislature to show that he is not in a position to 
pay the prescribed fee.” 

(4) Address.— -Candidates should give their present 
address and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of address

(6) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under any Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Damodar Valley Corporation), in 
India will be rejected unless they are submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service. 

Candidates serving under Government or a local or 
Statutory Body should submit an advance copy in the pres- 
cribed form. The application fee should in such cases be 
attached to the advance copy and not to the original. The 
candidature of such applicants may not however be con- 
sidered if the original applications do not reach the Com- 
mission's office within a fortnight from the closing date. 
Unless applications in original or advance copies with 
application fees are received within the closing date, late 
applications may be rejected.

iEME NO. LXX1II (AREA BETWEEN PARK 
CIRCUS AND LINTON STREET) 

s hereby notified under section 43 of the Calcutta 
irovement Act, 1911, that a General Improvement 
eme (to be known as Scheme No. LXXIII) for the 
pose of developing the area between Park Circus 
Linton Street by providing building sites, 
cdying defective ventilation, creating new or 
, roving existing means of communication and 
lities for traffic, affording better facilities for con- 
rancy and rehousing bustee-dwellers likely to be 
, laced, has been framed by the Board of Trustees 
the Improvement of Calcutta in the above area 
iin Wards Nos. 55 and 57 of the Corporation of 
:utta. 

!) The boundary of the area comprised in the 
shown within red verge on plan, is as 

;)ws : — 

On the North: Starting from the north-western 
corner of premises No. 55A, Beniapukur Road, 
running eastwards in a straight line to the north- 
eastern corner of plot No. 35, C.I.T. Scheme 
No. XLIX. 

On the East: From this point running south- 
wards in a straight line to south-eastern corner, 
of plot No. 27. C.I.T. Scheme XLIX; from this 
point running south-westwards in a straight line 
to the south-eastern corner of premises No. 33C, 
Gorachand Road; from this point running south- 
westwards in a straight line to the south-eastern 
corner of plot No. 6, C. I. T. Scheme No. XXXV. 

On the South: From this point running west- 
wards in a straight line to the southern corner 
of premises No. 1 Surhawardy Avenue; from 
this point running westwards in a straight line 
to the south-western corner of premises No. 191, 
Park Street. 


On the West: From this point running north- 
westwards in a straight line to the south-western 
corner of premises Nos. 26A, B and C, North 
Range; from this point running northwards in a 
straight line to the starting point. 

(3) Further particulars of the scheme, a plan show- 
ing the scheme area and a statement of the lands 
proposed for acquisition and for levy of betterment 
fee may be inspected at the office of the Trust at 

10 Netaji Subhas Road, Calcutta, between the hours 

11 a.m. and 3 p.m. on weekdays and between hours 
11 a.m. and 12-30 p.m. on Saturdays. 

Copies will be available on payment of the follow- 
ing fees: — 

Particulars and other information of the scheme 
— Re. 0.25 nP. 

Statement of lands proposed for acquisition or 
lor levy of betterment fee— Re. 0.25 nP. 

Plan of the scheme area — Re. 1.00 nP. 

(4) Objections to the Scheme will be received up to 
2nd July 1962. 

(5) Under section 6A of the Land Acquisition 
Act, 1894, as introduced by the Schedule to the 
Calcutta Improvement Act, 1911, as amended by the 
West Bengal Act XXXII of 1955, the publication of 
this notice shall have the same effect as the publica- 
tion of notification under section 4 of the Land 
Acquisition Act, 1894. 

K. SEN, 
Chairman.

NOTICE 

Calcutta, the 5th March 1962. 

Notice is hereby given under section 47(3) of the 
Calcutta Improvement Act, 1911, that the Board of 
Trustees for the Improvement of Calcutta have 
applied to the State Government for sanction to the 
Improvement Scheme No. LXXXII (Shyam Bose 
Road, Chetla) which was first published in the 
“Calcutta Gazette” and in local newspapers on the 
6th July 1961. 

K. SEN, Chairman.

Fourthly. -The medal shall be awarded for

displayed in saving life from drowning, fire and rescue 
operations in mines, etc. The extent of the meritori- 
ous acts of a humane nature to determine the class 
of the award shall be as follows: ~ 

Class l of the medal shall be awarded for con- 
spicuous courage under circumstances of very 
great danger to the life of the rescuer. 

Class II of the medal shall be awarded for courage 
and promptitude under circumstances of great 
danger to the life of the rescuer. 

Class III of the medal shall be awarded for courage 
and promptitude in saving life under circum- 
stances of grave bodily injury to the rescuer.

be worn.

worn on cei fain occasions by recipients shall be hall 
the size of the medal, and a sealed pattern ol the 
said miniature medal shall be deposited ana ktp . 


Twelfthly .— The President may cancel and annul 
the award of the medal to any person and thereupon 
the name of such recipient in the Register shall be 
erased and the recipient shall be required to surrender 
the insignia; but it shall be competent for the 
President to restore the decoration when such 
cancellation and annulment has been withdrawn.

members and creditors of the Company by necessary 
notice by publication in the “Calcutta Gazette" at an 
early date to finalise the above resol utiem."

TtfE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, APRIL 12, 1962 


The humble petition of the abovenained petitioner 
Mont respectfully sheweth : 


[Pam 14 


1. Your petitioner is a citizen of India and a person whose age was 
at all material times more than 25 years. Your petitioner is an elector as 
defined in clause (e) of section 2 of the Representation of the People Act, 
1951 (hereinafter referred to as “the said Act”) and is not subject to any 
of the disqualifications mentioned in section 16 of the Representation of the 
People Act, 1950. Your petitioner’s name is entered as Serial No. 208 in 
Part No. 102 in the electoral roll of the No. 146, Panchla Legislative 
Assembly Constituency in West Bengal. 


2. On the 19th day of February 1962 the general election of the matter 
of the State Legislature from the Panchla Legislative Assembly Constituency 
to the West Bengal Legislative Assembly took place. 


3. The names of the abovenamed Respondents were included in the 
relative or appropriate electoral roll as electors. 


4. The Respondents were candidates for election as a member of the 
West Bengal Legislative Assembly from the said Constituency. The symbols 
chosen by and allotted to the Re^pondonls under the Conduct of Election 
Rules, 1961, framed in exercise of the powers conferred by section 169 of the 
said Act, were as mentioned hereunder: — 


Respondent 'No. 1 — Lion. 

Respondent No. 2 — Two bullocks with yoke on. 
Respondent No. 3 — Star. 


5. On the 27th day of February 1962 the Returning Officer of the said 
constituency declared the result of the said election and 
returned the Respondent No. J as duly elected. In the return 
of election and in the final result sheet, 17,886 valid votes were shown to 
have been polled in favour of the Respondent No. 1, 17,867 in favour of the 
Respondent No. 2, and 1,255 in favour of the Respondent 'No. 3. The 
Respondent No. 1 purported to secure 19 votes more than those cast in favour 
of the Respondent No. 2. 


6. Your petitioner states that the purported election of the Respondent 
No. 1 is void, and liable to be set aside inter alia on* (he ground that the 
result of the said election, in so far as it concerned the Respondent No. 1 
has been materially affected by the improper reception of some votes and/or 
(he reception of votes which are void: — 


Particulars 


(a) The list of tendered votes in Form 15 prescribed by the Conduct of 
Election Rules, 1961, shows that some persons had posed themselves to be 
the real electors and personating the latter had cast voted, for which 41 
tendered votes of the real electors had not been or could not be counted for 
ascertainment ai*d declaration of the result of the election. The said 41 
bona fide electors, your petitioner understands and believes, have cast their 
votes in favour of the Respondent No. 2. 

(b) As far as your petitioner has been able to discover some persons had 
also personated for at least 18 dead electors and had purported to cast votes 
falsely representing themselves to be the voters on the electoral roll. Such 
votes your petitioner understands and believes have been cast in favour of 


Part LA.]

void, and that Respondent No. 2 the said Manilal Basu was duly 
elected and out to have been returned. 

And your petitioner, as in duty bound, shall ever pray.

TTie Commission accepts only the age of a candidate as

which she last attended, showing her exact age as 
recorded in the school register, 

2. An affidavit regarding her age sworn by her father 

or mother or some other person in a position to 
know by having been present or heard or her birth 
at the time of occurrence. * 


3. A certificate regarding her age, from a Member *

have known the candidate and her family, indul? 
ing clearly the evidence on the basis of which h 
she satisfied himself / herself on the point.

2. The attentum of the intending candidates is drawn 
to the rules regarding recruitment, to the West Bengal Civil

fications candidates are referred to the amendments of the

ELECTION COMMISSION, INDIA 
NOTIFICATION 

No. 82/36/62. llth April 1962. In pursuance oi 
the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 86 of the 
Representation oi the People Act, 1951, the Election 
Commission hereby publishes a copy of the Election 
Petition No. 36 of 1962, presented to the Com- 
mission on the 7th April 1962, under section 81 of 
the said Act, by Shri Nakul Chandra Sahis, mauza 
Bhutam, P.S. Puncha, P.O. Bhutam, district Purulia, 
calling in question the election to the Legislative 
Assembly of the State of West Bengal from the 
Jaipur constituency of that Assembly of Shri Adwaita 
Mandal, mauza Haludkanali, P.S. and P.O. 
Ranibundh, district Bankura. 

BEFORE I HE ELECTION COMMISSION, 
NEW DELHI 

In the Mattel of an election petition 
under the Representation of the People 
Act, 1951 

And 

In the Matter of purported election 
for Jaipur Legislative Assembly 
Constituency No. 203, Purulia, West 
Bengal, held on the 21st day of 
February 1962 

And 

In the Matter of Nakul Chandra Sahis, 
residing at mauza Bhutam, P.S. Puncha, 
P.O. Bhutam in the district of Purulia, 
Petitioner 

versus 

(1) Adwaita Mandal, falsely alleged to 
be a resident of mauza Haludkanali, 
P.S. and P.O. Ranibundh in the district 
of Bankura, but actually and ordinarily 
residing in mauza Sirishgora, P.S. 
Bandwan in the district of Purulia. 


(2) Prahlad Bauri residing at Munsif- 
danga in the town of Purulia, district 
Purulia. 

(3) Bishnu Charan Das, residing in 
mauza Nadiara, P.S. Purulia, P.O. 
Nadiara, in the district of Purulia. 

(4) Keshari Rajowar, residing in mauza 
Dumdum, P.S. Purulia, P.O. Chharra 
in the district of Purulia. 

(5) Jajneswar Das, resident of Alanngi- 
danga, P.O. and P.S. Purulia, 
Respondents. 

The humble petition of the above- 
named petitioner 

Most respectfully sheweth: 

1. Your petitioner is a citizen of India and a 
person whose age was at all material times more 
than 25 years. Your petitioner is an elector as 
defined in clause (e) of section 2 of the Representa- 
tion of the People Act, 1951 (hereinafter referred to 
as the “said Ad”), and is not subject to any of the 
disqualifications mentioned in section 16 of the 
Representation of the People Act, 1950. Your 
petitioner's name is duly entered in the electoral roll 
of the Manbazar Legislative Assembly Constituency 
in the district of Purulia. Your petitioner possesses 
all qualifications for membership of the State 
Legislatures as prescribed by or under the 
Constitution of India or any law made by the 
Parliament. 

2. On the 21st day of February 1962 the general 
election of a member of the State Legislature from 
the scat of the Jaipur Legislative Assembly 
Constituency (reserved for Scheduled castes), to the 
West Bengal Legislative Assembly took place. 

3. Your petitioner and the respondents were the 
only contesting candidates for election as a member 
of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly from the 
said Constituency. The symbols chosen by and

SCHEME No. LXXXV (SUBHAS SAROBAR) 

1. It is notified under section 43 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act that a General Improvement 
Scheme to be known as Scheme No, LXXXV 
(Subhas Sarobar) for the area ol Scheme 1VM 
(Supplementary) in Constituency No. 36 of the 
Calcutta Corporation, to provide for a lake, parks 
and gardens, open space and playgrounds and pro- 
vision therein of recreation building and structures 
and other necessary aids to field and aquatic sports 
including a swimming area and a swimming pool, 
a boat-house, construction of roads, pathways and 
cycle track and other developments, has been 
framed by the Board of Trustees for the Improve- 
ment of Calcutta. 

2. The boundary of the area comprised within 
and affected by the Scheme shown within red 
verge on the plan is as follows: — 

On the North: Starting from the north-easterrt 
corner of 75 Narkeldanga Main Road running 
eastwards along the southern edge of Narkel- 
danga Main Road, western, southern and eastern 
boundaries of premises No. 81 Narkeldanga 
Main Road, again eastward along the 
southern edge of Narkeldanga Main Road, 
to its eastern end where it meets the western 
boundary of Calcutta Corporation pumping 
station on New Cut Canal surplus land. 

On the East: From this point running south** 
ward along the western boundaries of canal 
surplus land to a point where it meets the 
western edge of Radhamadhab Dutta Garden 
Lane. From this point running southward 
along the western edge of Radhamadhab Dutta 
Garden Lane to the north-eastern corner of 
No. 58, Suren Sarkar Road. Then westward 
and southward along the northern and western 
boundaries of the said premises to its south- 
western corner. 

On the South: From this point running west- 
ward along the northern edge of Suren Sarkar 
Road, the eastern and northern boundaries of 
45B Suren Sarkar Road, northern and western 
boundaries of 45A Suren Sarkar Road and again 
along the northern edge of Suren Sarkar Road 
to a point situated at a distance of 56 ft. from 
the north-western corner of 21/1 Surah 3rd 
Lane and then running south-westward across 
Suren Sarkar Road to the north-western corner 
of 21/1 Surah 3rd Lane then along the western 
and southern boundaries of the said premises 
to its south-eastern corner, then southwards 
along the western edge of Surah 3rd Lane to a 
distance of 320 ft. then westward to a point 
on the eastern boundary of plot 56 in Scheme

SCHEME No. LXXXV (SUBHAS SAROBAR) 

1. It is notified under section 43 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act that a General Improvement 
Scheme to be known as Scheme No. LXXXV 
(Subhas Sarobar) for the area ot Scheme 1VM 
(Supplementary) in Constituency No. 36 of the 
Calcutta Corporation, to provide for a lake, parks 
and gardens, open space and playgrounds and pro- 
vision therein of recreation building and structures 
and other necessary aids to field and aquatic sports 
including a swimming area and a swimming pool, 
a boat-house, construction of roads, pathways and 
cycle track and other developments, has been 
framed by the Board of Trustees for the Improve- 
ment of Calcutta. 

2. The boundary of the area comprised within 
and affected by the Scheme shown within red 
verge on the plan is as follows: ■

corner of 75 Narkeldanga Main Road running

boundaries of premises No. 81 Narkeldanga 
Main Road, again eastward along the 
southern edge of Narkeldanga Main Road, 
to its eastern end where it meets the western 
boundary of Calcutta Corporation pumping 
station on New Cut Canal surplus land.

ward along the western boundaries of canal 
surplus land to a point where it meets the

Lane. From this point running southward 
along the western edge of Radhamadhab Dutta 
Garden Lane to the north-eastern corner of 
No. 58, Suren Sarkar Road. Then westward 
and southward along the northern and western 
boundaries of the said premises to its south- 
western corner. 

On the South: From this point running west*

GENERAL ADMINISTRATION DEPARTMENT 

NOTIFICATION 

Sachivalaya, Ahmedabad, the 22nd March 1962 
(Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.) 

No. BAP-2659/366-A2. — Whereas it appears to 
the Government of Gujarat that the book, named 
“Chandralila'\, translated into Gujarati from English 
by Rev. Dr. H. R. Scott, printed and published for 
the Gujarat Tract and Book Society by Rev. II. P. 
Cromic, at the Darshana Printery, Nagori Shala, 
Ratanpolc, Ahmedabad 1, contains matter which 
promotes feelings of hatred between different classes 
of citizens of India and that its publication is punish- 
able under section 153-A of the Indian Penal Code. 

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers con- 
ferred by section 99A of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898), the Government of 
Gujarat hereby declares every copy of the aforesaid 
book to be forfeited to Government. 

By order and in the name of the 
Governor of Gujarat, 
ft. PARTHASARATHY, Under Secy.

Calcutta Corporation, to provide for a lake, parks 
‘ j gardens, open space and playgrounds and pro- 
ision therein of recreation building and structures 
other necessary aids to field and aquatic sports 
Deluding a swimming area and a swimming pool, 
j boat-house, construction of roads, pathways and 
nek track and other developments, has been 
framed by the Board of Trustees for the Improve- 
ment of Calcutta. 

2. The boundary of the area comprised within 
and affected by the Scheme shown within red 
verge on the plan is as follows:— 

On the North: Starting from the north-eastern 
corner of 75 Narkeldanga Main Road running 
eastwards along the southern edge of Narkel- 
danga Main Road, western, southern and eastern 
boundaries of premises No. 81 Narkeldanga 
Main Road, again eastward along the 
southern edge of Narkeldanga Main Road, 
to its eastern end where it meets the western 
boundary of Calcutta Corporation pumping 
station on New Cut Canal surplus land. 

On the East: From this point running south- 
ward along the western boundaries of canal 
surplus land to a point where it meets the 
western edge of Radhamadhab Dutta Garden 
Lane. From this point running southward 
along the western edge of Radhamadhab Dutta 
Garden Lane to the north-eastern corner of 
No. 58, Suren Sarkar Road. Then westward 
and southward along the northern and western 
boundaries of the said premises to its south- 
western corner. 

On the South: From this point running west- 
ward along the northern edge of Suren Sarkar 
Hoad, the eastern and northern boundaries of 
Suren Sarkar Road, northern and western 
boundaries of 45A Suren Sarkar Road and again 
along the northern edge of Suren Sarkar Road 
to a point situated at a distance of 56 ft. F*om 
the north-western corner of 21/1 Surah 3rd 
Lane and then running south-westward across 
Suren Sarkar Road to the north-western corner 
of 21/1 Surah 3rd Lane then along the western 
and southern boundaries of the said premises 
to its south-eastern corner, then southwards 
along the western edge of Surah 3rd Lane to a 
distance of 320 ft. then westward to a point 
the eastern boundary of plot 56 in Scheme 
1V M, situated at a distance of 20 ft. to the 


south from its north-eastern corner, then north- 
ward along its eastern boundary to its north- 
eastern corner, then westward along the 
northern boundary of plot 56, eastern and 
northern boundaries of plot Nos. 53, 48 and 47, 
Scheme 1VM respectively, and the northern 
boundary of plot No. 45, Scheme IVM, then 
across 100 ft. C.I.T. Road to a point on the 
eastern boundary of 38 Badan Roy Lane, at 
a distance of 80 ft. to the south from its north- 
eastern corner, then to its north-eastern corner 
and then westward along its northern boundary 
to the point where it meets the eastern edge 
ol Badan Roy Lane. 

On the West: From this point running north- 
ward along the eastern edge of Badan Roy 
Lane to its northern end where it meets the 
southern edge of Suren Sarkar Road, then 
eastward along the southern edge of Suren 
Sarkar Road to a distance of 244 It. then across 
Suren Sarkar Road northward along the 
eastern, northern and again eastern edge of the 
Calcutta Corporation passage to its northern 
end, and then across it and along the eastern 
boundaries of Premises No. 34G, 34F and ME, 
Suren Sarkar Road and 75 Narkeldanga Main 
Road to the starting point. 

3. Particulars and other information relating to 
the Scheme and a plan of the area comprised in the 
scheme may be inspected at the office of the Trust 
at 10 Netaji Subhas Road, Calcutta, between 11 a.m. 
and 3 p.m. on weekdays and between 11 a.m. and 
12 noon on Saturdays. 

All lands required for execution of the scheme 
have already bee// acquired in connection with 
Calcutta Improvement Trust’s Scheme No. IVM 
(Supplementary).

Particulars of the scheme and other informa- 
tion relating thereto — Rs. 0.25 nP.

“B” 

(Translated into English) 


Sucta, 

As Sulam Alakum P.O. Amrargaih, 

Burdwan. 

As a question may arise in your mind as to why 
1 left the Congress after remaining in it for these 
long days, 1 feci it necessary to explain the reasons. 

Firstly, in the first General Elections after the 
country became independent, the Congress gave 
nominations to three Muslims from the district of 
Burdwan. In the second General Elections, two 
Muslims were given nominations by the Congress. 
But in the impending General Elections, only one 
person has been given nomination and it was because 
he is a Minister. Even after that, lest he wins, 
another Congressman has been made to stand against 
him so as to get him defeated. To remain attached 
with such an anti-Muslim District Congress would 
be an inconsiderate act and hence, as a protest, I 
have resigned. 

Secondly, ail the Congress workers of Kanksa and 
Ausgram Police Stations demanded for giving 
Congress nomination for the Ausgram Constituency 
to any person from the Ausgram Centre; but 
unfortunately, that demand was neglected by the 
District Congress, and my protest against the same 
is the second reason of my leaving the Congress. 


You arc wise men and will consider the whole 
after with all your wisdom. 

Yours since rely, 
(Sd.) ABDUL KADLp 


Jonah Abdul Wahen Khah, 
Bhatkunda, 

P.O. Bhatkunda, 

Dist. Burdwan.

CALCUTTA IMPROVEMENT TRUST 
NOTICE 

NOTICE is hereby given under section 47(3) of the 
Calcutta Improvement Act, 1911, that the Board of 
Trustees for the Improvement of Calcutta have 
«mlied to the State Government for sanction to the 
toprovement Scheme No. LXXXIV (Park at 138 
Cornwallis Street) which was first published in the 
“Calcutta Gazette” and in local newspapers on the 
12th October 1961. 

10 Netaji Subhas Road, Calcutta-1 
The 5th April 1962. 

K. SEN, Chairman. 


NOTIFICATION 

Repayment of 4 per cent. Calcutta Improvement 
Trust Debenture Loan of 1952, dated the 25th 
August 1952. 

The 4 per cent. Calcutta Improvement Trust 
Debenture Loan of 25 th August 1952 for 
Rs. 80,00,000 is repayable on the 25th August 1962 
from which date interest on it will cease. Holders 
of Debentures of this loan should tender their 
Debentures at the Local Authorities Loan Section, 


State Bank of India, Calcutta, at least three weeks 
before the due date of repayment with the follow- 
ing endorsement on the back of each Debenture: — 

“Received payment in full of all demand for 
principal and interest hereon. 

10, Netaji Subhas Road, 

Calcutta-1. 

The 23rd April 1962. 


Signature of Holder.” 

K. SEN, 
Chairman.

“14E”.

ELECTION COMMISSION, INDIA 

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 3rd May 1962. 

No. 82/140/62. — In pursuance of the provisions 
of sub-section (1) of section 86 of the Representation 
ol the. People Act, 1951, the Election Commission 
hereby publishes a copy of the Election Petition 
No. 140 of 1962, presented to the Commission on the 
11th April 1962, under section 81 of the said Act, 
by Shri Amalendra Lai Roy, son of Shashi Lai Roy, 
Kandi, post office and police-station Kandi, district 
Murshidabad, West Bengal, calling in question the 
election to the Legislative Assembly of the State of 
West Bengal from the Kandi constituency of that 
Assembly of Kumar Jagadish Chandra Sinha, son of 
late Birendra Chandra Sinha, Kandi Rajbati, post 
^tice and police-station Kandi, district Murshidabad, 
West Bengal. 

Election Petition No. 140 of 1962 

To THE ELECTION COMMISSION, INDIA, 

1 Aurangzeb Road, 

New Delhi. 

n the matter of an election petition under the 
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Act 
43 of 1951) 

And 

* n the matter of calling into the question the Election 
held in February 1962 for filling a seat in the 
West Bengal Legislative Assembly from 50 
, an di Assembly Constituency and declaring the 
ejection of Kumar Jagadish Chandra .Sinha as 
the returned candidate from the said 

Constituency to be void and further declaring 
that Amalendra Lai Roy has been duly 


elected to fill the seat in the West Bengal 
Legislative Assembly lrom 50 Kandi Assembly 
Constituency 

And 

In the matter of Amalendra Lai Roy, son of Shashi 
Lai Roy, of Kandi, post office and police-station 
Kandi, district Murshidabad, West Bengal, 
Petitioner. 

versus 

Kumar Jagadish Chandra Sinha, son of late Birendra 
Chandra Sinha, of Kandi Rajbati, post office and 
police-station Kandi, district Murshidabad, West 
Bengal, Respondent. 

The humble petition of the aforesaid 

petitioner, 

Most respectfully sheweth: 


(1) That your petitioner is a voter in the 50— 
Kandi Assembly Constituency and his name 
appears in the Electoral Roll maintained for the said 
50 -Kandi Assembly Constituency in Part 60, Serial 
No. 8, as finally published and that your petitioner 
offered himself as a candidate for election to fill a 
seat in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly from 
the said Constituency held on 20th February 1962. 

(2) That the aforesaid respondent also offered 
himself as a candidate for a seat in the West Bengal 
Legislative Assembly from the same Constituency 
and was illegally declared as duly elected to fill the 
seat in the above Constituency by Shri N. K. Saha, 
Returning Officer of the said Constituency, on the 
27th of February 1962. 

(3) That on the 27th of February 1962 the date 
appointed for the counting of votes in the said 50 — 
Kandi Assembly Constituency, after the completion 
of the counting of votes polled by this petitioner 
and the abovenamed respondent, the aforesaid 


84 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, MAY 17, 1962 


[Part 


Returning Officer recorded in the Result-sheet in 
Form 20, the total number of votes polled by each 
candidate and announced the same, after which 
Shri Suhas Das, election agent of this petitioner, 
applied in writing to the said Returning Officer for 
a recount of all the ballot papers already counted, 
stating the grounds on which he demanded such 
recount (certified copy of the petition is filed here- 
with marked as Annexure A). 

(4) That the said Returning Officer illegally 
rejected the prayer for recounting made at the 
appropriate time as required by rule 63(3) of the 
Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, on grounds which 
are bad both in facts as well as in law and assigned 
such reasons for this rejection which contravene the 
provisions of rule 63 of the Conduct of Election 
Rules, 1961, which deal with the “Recount of 
Votes”. 

That rule 63(1) of the Conduct of Election Rules, 
1961, clearly lays down that a candidate or his 
election agent may apply in writing for a recount of 
all or any of the ballot papers already counted only 
after the completion of counting and the announce- 
ment of the total nugiber of votes polled by each 
candidate by the Returning Officer and that the 
prayer of the election agent of this petitioner for 
recount was made in accordance with the provisions 
of the relevant rule. 

That neither the Representation of the People Act, 
1951, nor the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, gives 
to any candidate, or his Election Agent, or counting 
agents any right or scope to raise any objection 
about the results ol counting, or to demand a recount 
of all or any of the ballot papers already counted, at 
any earlier stage of counting of the ballot papers in 
any election, for any Assembly or Parliamentary 
Constituency before the completion of the counting 
of votes recorded in all the ballot papers, the 
recording in the result-sheet in Form 20 of the total 
number of votes polled by each candidate and the 
announcement of the same by the Returning Officer. 

That the failure of this petitioner and his election 
agent to raise any objection at earlier stages of 
counting on the 27th of February 1962, the appointed 
date for counting of votes for the said 50 — Kandi 
Assembly Constituency, and the fact that the 
application for recount was made on that date by 
the election agent of this petitioner only after the 
completion of the counting of all the ballot papers 
and announcements of the aggregated total of votes 
polled by each candidate, were assigned by the 
Returning Officer as the reasons for finding the 
prayer for recount as being unreasonable. 

(A certified copy of the order passed by the 
Returning Officer on the application of Shri 
Suhas Das, Election Agent of this petitioner, 
on 27th February 1962 at 4-15 p.m. is attached 
herewith marked as Annexure B.) 

(5) That the counting of votes for the said 50 — 
Kandi Assembly Constituency started at 9 a.m. on 
27th February 1962 and was completed at about 
3-20 p.m. That 42,746 ballot papers (including 
42,614 votes recorded at polling stations and 132 
ballot papers sent by post) were scrutinised and 
counted within a very short period of six hours and 


20 minutes (i.e., from 9 a.m. to 3-20 p.m.) very 
hurriedly without giving this petitioner and his 
counting agents sufficient opportunities of following 
the scrutiny and rejection of ballot papers and 
reception and counting of valid ballot papers and 
without leaving any time and scope for making 
objections regarding irregularities and illegalities 
committed during the very hurried procedure of 
counting. 

(6) That the Returning Officer erred in law i n 
following the procedure laid down in rule 56A of the 
Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, which is applicable 
only to the scrutiny and rejection of ballot papers in 
the counting of votes at notified polling stations 
under rule 59 of the said Rules, but is not applicable 
to the scrutiny and rejection of ballot papers in the 
present case. 

(7) That the procedure adopted by the Returning 
Officer resulted in the improper reception, refusal or 
rejection of votes and reception of votes which are 
void, materially affecting the result of the election. 

That if the votes are recounted and the validity 
of ballot papers is scrutinised legally and properly 
this petitioner will be found to have secured greater 
number of votes than the abovementioned respondent 
and will be found to have been duly elected to fill 
the seat in the Kandi Assembly Constituency. 

(8) That excluding the postal ballot papers this 
petitioner is recorded to have polled 20,286 votes and 
the respondent 20,297 votes and there was thus a 
difference of very small margin of votes numbering 
only 11 (eleven) between this petitioner and the 
respondent in respect of votes recorded at polling 
stations. That the observation made by the 

Returning Officer “ The margin between the 

candidates is not narrow inasmuch as there is a 

difference of 94 votes ” is not substantially 

correct, because the number of votes recorded by 
postal ballots as well as the recorded overall 
difference of 94 votes between the petitioner and the 
respondent is only a fractional percentage of the 
total number of votes polled. 

(9) That after the rejection of the prayer of 
recount and the passing of his order onjt at 
4-15 p.m. the said Returning Officer completed and 
signed the Final Result-sheet in Form 20 and there- 
after illegally declared the abovementioned respondent 
as duly elected to fill the seat in the West Bengal 
Legislative Assembly from the 50 — Kandi Assembly 
Constituency. 

(A certified copy of the declaration of election 
to the West Bengal Legislative Assembly, 
50 — Kandi Assembly Constituency, is filed 
herewith marked as Annexure C.) 

(10) That the voting in the election for the 
50— Kandi Assembly Constituency was very close as 
between this petitioner and the respondent inasmuch 
as the respondent is recorded to have won by a very 
narrow margin of votes and that there are as se 
forth above good grounds to believe that the 
counting of the ballot papers was not in order an 
that the final figures as noted by the Returning 
Officer have been affected by miscount on his par 
and that it is therefore highly desirable to have 
recount in this case for the ends of justice.

THE COMMISSIONERS FOR THE PORT OF 
CALCUTTA 


Summary of the Mlnutea of tho Proceeding* of the 
U Commissioners’ 2nd (Special) and 3rd Meetings held 
on the 26th February 1082. 

VP the 2nd (Special) Meeting of the Commissioners held 
on the 20th February 19G2, the revised estimates tor 
1901-02 and the budget estimates tor 1902-03 were 
sanctioned subject to the sanction oi Government. 

I Revised estimate* for 1961-62: The revised estimate 
oi the total income for the year amounted to 
Its 14,29,88,850 - against the original estimate ot 
Its 14 11 27.073 while the revised estimate oi the total 
expenditure was Its. 13,9:1,44 050 against the ongma 
estimate of Rs. 14,38,07,424. Thus the year was expected 
to close with a surplus of Its. 30,44.800 against a surplus 
ol Rs. 2,00,249 only foreshadowed by the original 
estimates. 

II. Budget estimates Of 1962-63: The total sea-borne 
traffic likely to pass through the Port during 1902-63 was 
taken as 10,160,000 metric tonnes and the income as 
Rs 14 89,70,650. The total expenditure for the year was 
estimated at Rs. 14,87,10,240 and the year was expected to 
close with a surplus of Rs. 2,00,404. 

At the 3rd Meeting of the Commissioners held on tho 
20th February 1902, tho following business was 
transacted: — 

1 Purchase and installation of plant and machinery at 
the Kidderpore Dry Docks and King George’s Dock, Loco 
Shed and other Workshops, No. 8 Workshop and No. 14 
Berth, Kldderpore Docks— Third Five-Year Plan: The 

Commissioners sanctioned subject to the sanction ot 
Government as a charge to Capital an estimate oi Rs. lo 
lakhs for the above work. 


2. Revision of tho pay scales of Class III and Class IV 
employees In the light of the Second Pay Commissions 
reoommendations, as adopted by Government: The Com- 
missioners approved the revised scales of pay for Class III 
and Class IV employees with retrospective effect from tho 
lBt July 1969. 


3 Payment of caloutta compensatory allowance to 
dlreotly recruited Class I non-Marlne Officers of the Com- 
missloners: The Commissioners sanctioned subject w> > he 
sanction of Government, the payment of Calcutta compen- 
satory allowance to all those Class I service officers m i lie* 
non-marine services ol the Commissioners who wcie 
recruited direct after 23rd .November 1948 with effect from 
the 1st July 1959, the date of implementation of the 
Second Pay Commission’s recommendations. 

4. Continuance of the practioe of observing half holidays 
on Saturdays — Recommendation of Second Pay Commis- 
sion: The Commissioners approved the Special Committees 
recommendation to continue the existing practice ot 
observing Saturday as half working day. 

5. Adoption of pension scheme for the Commissioners 
empolyees: The Commissioners sanctioned subject to the 
sanction of Government the Chairman’s recommendation 
in the matter. 

0. Retrospective effect to the introduction of the Incen- 
tive Tonnage Scheme: The Commissioners approwd ,ho 
payment of at rears of wages consequent on the introduc- 
tion ot the Incentive Tonnage Scheme with retrospective 
effect from the 20th July 1901. 

7. Special establishment for dealing with the construc- 
tion of new craft under the Third Five-Year Plan: Tin- 
Commissioners sanctioned subject to the sanction oi 
Government the creation of certain posts on a temporary 
basis for a period of three years with effect from the 1st 
April 1902 as recommended by the Deputy Conservator. 

8. Block proposals: The Commissioners also sanctions! 
routine establishment proposals and routine proposals 
relating to execution of works, grant of leases, purchase oi 
material, remission of eharges ete.

SUPPLEMENT TO THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, MAY 24, 1962 


175 


THE board of trustees for the improve- 

1 MENT OF CALCUTTA 

Notice under section 43 of the Calcutta Improvement 
n Act, 1911 (Bengal Act V of 1911) 

BUSTEE REHOUSING SCHEME No. X 

1. it is hereby notified, under section 43 of the 
Calcutta Improvement Act, that an Improvement 
Scheme, namely, a Housing Accommodation Scheme, 
for the purpose of affording alternative residential 
accommodation to bustee dwellers who may be 
displaced from their residence by the acquisition of 
bustees by the Trust for Scheme Nos. VI-M (Supple- 
mentary) and VI1I-M and other Improvement 
Schemes and to be hereafter known as Bustee 
Rehousing Scheme No. X has been framed by the 
Board of Trustees for the Improvement of Calcutta 
in Constituency No. 16 of the Calcutta Corporation. 

2. The area comprised within and required for 
the execution of the Scheme (shown in yellow verge 
in the plan) measures 7.24 acres more or less and is 
more particularly described below: — 

Boundaries of the land 

On the North: Starting from the south-western 
corner of the premises No. 52 Bagmari Road 
(Mohammedan Burial Ground) running east- 
ward along its southern boundary up to the 
north-western corner of the premises No. 120- 
A, Manicktala Main Road. 

On the East: From this point running southward, 
westward and then southward along the 
western boundary of premises No. 120 A, 
Manicktala Main Road to the north-eastern 
corner of the Subsidised Industrial Housing 
Scheme No. IV, within C.I.T. Scheme VII-M. 

On the South: From this point running westward 
along the northern boundary of the Subsidised 
Industrial Housing Scheme No. IV to its north- 
western corner, then southward along its 
western boundary for a distance of 31 feet then 
westward in a straight line for a distance of 


90 feet to a point on the eastern edge of 120 
feet New C.I.T. Road situated at a distance of 
96 feet to the south-west from the north- 
western corner of the Subsidised Industrial 
Housing Scheme No. IV. 

On the West: From this point running north- 
ward along the eastern edge of 120 feet C.I.T. 
Road for a distance of 104 feet then eastward 
for a distance of 90 feet to a point situated 
at a distance of 75 feet to the north from the 
north-western corner of the Subsidised Indus- 
trial Housing Scheme No. IV, then running 
northward in a straight line for a distance of 
465 feet to a point situated at a distance of 
98 feet on the south-east from the south- 
western corner of 52, Bagmari Road, then 
westwards for a distance of 90 feet to a point 
on the eastern edge of 120 feet C.I.T. Road 
situated at a distance of 30 feet to the south 
of south-western corner of 52, Bagmari Road, 
then northward along the eastern edge of 120 
feet C.I.T, Road to the starting point. 

3. Particulars of the scheme and a 
map of the area comprised in the 
scheme may be seen at the office of the Calcutta 
Improvement Trust at 10 Netaji Subhas Road, 
Calcutta-1, on week days between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. 
and on Saturdays between 11 a.m. and 12 noon. All 
the lands required for the execution of the scheme 
have already been or will be acquired in connection 
with Calcutta Improvement Trust Scheme No. VII-M. 

Copies of the above documents will be available on 
payment of the following fees: — 

Particulars of the scheme — Re. 0.25 nP. 

Plan of the .scheme area and layout of the scheme 
— Rs. 1.00 nP. 

4. Objections will be received by the Chairman 
up to 28th June 1962. 

K. SEN, Chairman. 
Dated, Calcutta, the 7th May 1962.

5. A booklet was published by Shri Binoy Roy,

Part II] 


Candidates in Government service Bhould make sure 
before depositing fee that their application* will be forward- 
34 by their superior officers. In no case will the fee paid 
with the application be refunded. 

The Commission may remit fee in case of genuine 
indigent and bona fide displaced person from Pakistan. 

An indigent displaced person shall, in the first instance, 
p B y the application fee prescribed for a gazetted post 
advertised by the Commission but if he / she is selected for 
and appears at the interview, the fee paid by him/her will 
be refunded afterwards. 

Note* — “(i) A displaced person claiming age concession 
must turnish with his application satisfactory evidence 
that he is bona fide displaced person from Pakistan, e.g 
refugee registration card or a certificate from a gazetted 
officer or a Member of Parliament or State Legislature, in 
original. 

(li) A member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled 
Tribe claiming age concession must furnish with his appli- 
cation a certificate in original from a gazetted officer or a 
Member of Parliament or State Legislature belonging to 
the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, specifying the 
particular caste or tribe to which he claims to belong. 

(in) A displaced person seeking remission of the applica- 
tion fee must furnish besides the evidence required under 
Note (i) above, a certificate (in original) from a District 
Officer or a gazetted officer or » Member of Parliament or 
State Legislature to show that he is not in a position to 
pay the prescribed fee.” 

(4) Address. — Candidates should give their present 
address and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of address. 

(5) Canvassing. — Any attempt on the part of candidates 
to enlist support of their applications through persons of 
influence or officials of Government will disqualify them 
for appointment. Spontaneous recommendation from 
persona interested in the candidates or otherwise known 
to them will be disregarded. 

(6) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under any Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Damodar Valley Corporation), in 
India will lie rejected unless they are submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service. 

Candidates serving under Government or a local or 
Statutory Body should submit an advance copy in the pres- 
cribed form. The application fee should in such cases be 
attached to the advance copy and not to the original. The 
candidature of such applicants may not however be con- 
sidered if the original applications do not reach the Com- 
mission’s office within a fortnight from the closing date. 
Unless applications in original or advance copies with 
application fees are received within the closing date, late 
applications may be rejected.

SUPPLEMENT TO THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, MAY 31, 1962

the board of trustees for the improve. 

MENT OF CALCUTTA 


Notice under section 43 of the Calcutta Improvement 
Act, 1911 (Bengal Act V of 1911) 

BUSTEE REHOUSING SCHEME No. X 

1. It is hereby notified, under section 41 of the 
Calcutta Improvement Act, that an Improvement 
Scheme, namely, a Housing Accommodation Scheme, 
for the purpose of affording alternative residential 
accommodation to bustee dwellers who may be 
displaced from their residence by the acquisition of 
bustees by the Trust for Scheme Nos. VI-M (Supple- 
mentary) and VIII-M and other Improvement 
Schemes and to be hereafter known as Bustee 
Rehousing Scheme No. X has been framed by the 
Board of Trustees for the Improvement of Calcutta 
in Constituency No. 16 of the Calcutta Corporation. 

2. The area comprised within and required for 
the execution of the Scheme (shown in yellow verge 
in the plan) measures 7.24 acres more or less and is 
more particularly described below: — 

Boundaries of the land 

On the North: Starting from the south-western 
corner of the premises No. 52 Bagmari Road 
(Mohammedan Burial Ground) running east- 
ward along its southern boundary up to the 
north-western corner of the premises No. 120- 
A, Manicktala Main Road. 

On the East: From this point running southward, 
westward and then southward along the 
western boundary of premises No. 120A, 
Manicktala Main Road to the north-eastern 
corner of the Subsidised Industrial Housing 
Scheme No. IV, within C.I.T. Scheme VII-M. 

On the South: From this point running westward 
along the northern boundary of the Subsidised 
Industrial Housing Scheme No. IV to its north- 
western corner, then southward along its 
western boundary for a distance of 31 feet then 
westward in a straight line for a distance of 


90 feet to a point on the- eastern edge of 120 
feet New C.I.T. Road situated at a distance of 
96 feet to the south-west from the north- 
western comer of the Subsidised Industrial 
Housing Scheme No. IV. 

On the West: From this point running north- 
ward along the eastern edge of 120 feet C.I.T. 
Road for a distance of 104 feet then eastward 
for a distance of 90 ieet to a point situated 
at a distance of 75 feet to the north from the 
north-western corner of the Subsidised Indus- 
trial Housing Scheme No. IV, then running 
northward in a straight line for a distance of 
465 leet to a point situated at a distance of 
98 feet on the south-east from the south- 
western corner of 52, Bagmari Road, then 
westwards for a distance of 90 feet to a point 
on the eastern edge of 120 feet C.I.T. Road 
situated at a distance of 30 feet to the south 
of south-western corner of 52, Bagmari Road, 
then northward along the eastern edge of 120 
feet C.I.T. Road to the starting point. 

3. Particulars of the scheme and a 
map of the area comprised in the 
scheme may be seen at the office of the Calcutta 
Improvement Trust at 10 Netaji Subhas Road, 
Calcutta-1, on week days between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. 
and on Saturdays between 11 a.m. and 12 noon. All 
the lands required for the execution of the scheme 
have already been or will be acquired in connection 
with Calcutta Improvement Trust Scheme No. VII-M. 

Copies of the above documents will be available on 
payment of the following fees: — 

Particulfrs of the scheme— Re. 0.25 nP. 

Plan of the scheme area and layout of the scheme 
— Rs. 1.00 nP. 

4. Objections will be received by the Chairman 
up to 28th June 1962. 

K. SEN, Chairman. 
Dated, Calcutta, the 7th May 1962.

Orders by the Governor 
Political Department 

Shillong, the 28th April 1962. 

No. PLA.8/62/Pt.I/8. — Whereas the Governor of 
Assam is satisfied that the article under caption 
“Asomoloi Nababor Agoman” published in the 
issue of 13th April 1962 of “Asorn Bani”, a weekly 
newspaper of Gauhati, edited by Shri Satish Chandra 
Kakoti and printed at Tribune Press, Gauhati, con- 
tains matters which promote and are intended to 
promote feelings of enmity and hatred between 
different classes of citizens of India, e.g., the Ahoms 
and the Muslims. 

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred 
by section 99A, Cr.P.C., 1898 (Act V of 1898), the 
Governor of Assam is pleased to declare every copy 
of the aforesaid publication to be forfeited to Govern- 
ment. 

A. N. KIDWAI, Chief Secy.

CORPORATION OF CALCUTTA 

NOTICE 

NOTICE is hereby given for information of the public 
that the Corporation of Calcutta at their meeting 
heki on the 1st June 1962, adopted the following 
Rules framed under sub-section (5) of section 527 
read with sub-sections (2) and (4) of section 281 of 
the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, for the use of 
Corporation water for washing vehicles kept for 
protit, saie or hire as stated herein below: — 

Rules under sub-section 5 of section 527 read with 
sub-sections (2) and (4) of section 281 of the 
Calcutta Municipal Act of 1951 and section 54 
of the Calcutta Municipal (Amendment) Act, 
1953, for the use of Corporation Water for wash- 
ing carts kept for profit, sale or hire. 

This may be called rules under sub-section 5 of 
section 527 read with sub-section (2) and sub-section 

(4) of section 281 of the Calcutta Municipal Act of 
195k section 54 of the Calcutta Municipal (Amend- 
ment) Act, 1953) and are to come into effect from a 
date the Commissioner, Calcutta Corporation, may 
decide. *■— 

(1) Vehicles propelled by power, drav\n by 
aminals or human beings excepting bullock and 
buffalo carts and rickshaws and those owned and 
used by the Military, kept or used in Calcutta for 
sa.j. profit or hire should be deemed as using, unless 
otherwise proved to the satisfaction of the Commis- 
^•aer, filtered, unfiltcrcd or tubewell water of the 
Corporation for washing the same without being 
authorised as envisaged under sections 270 and 271 of 
the Calcutta Municipal Act of 1951. 

(2i Poisons, institutions, commercial concerns, 
departments of the Government using Corporation 
vwsrer for washing vehicles kept for sale, profit or hire 
s bal! be liable to pay to the Corporation on the basis 
of individual vehicles at rates prescribed hereinbelow 
under sub-section (2) of section 281 of the Calcutta 
Municipal Act, 1951: — 

Per financial year. 


(5) An additional fee of 25 per cent, shall be 
imposed on the assessee if he does not make pay- 
ment of the demand within a month from the date of 
receipt of the notice referred to above or fails to put 
lortn sufficient reason for non-payment to the satis- 
faction of the Commissioner within the said time. 

(6) (a) Institutions, commercial concerns and 
departments of the Government shall forward to the 
Corporation in the months of May and November 
each year Statements, containing description of all 
vehicles kept or used by them in Calcutta and liable 
to be charged and at the same time deposit to the 
Corporation the amount due for the vehicles if it was 
not made at any previous date.
