PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, WEST BENGAL 

eneral Instructions to candidates applying in response to 
advertisements issued by the Commission for recruit- 
ment to posts of “Selection". 

(l) Instructions regarding submission of application. - 

ipphcations are to he made on the prescribed term which 
nil be available from the office of the Public Service Oora- 
ussion, West Bengal, Anderson House (ground floor), 
dipore, Calcutta-27, personally or on sending a large self- 
ddressecl envelope with stamps sufficient to cover the 
Kxitage affixed to it. Candidates who are unable to obtain 
opieK of the prescribed form may apply on any similar 
ypeil (not handwritten) form showing exactly the word- 
iiff and spacing of the sample form published in the 
Calcutta Gazette” of the 1st September 1955, provided 
he blanks are filled up in the candidates’ own handwriting. 

W) Particulars and oartlfioates required.— Candidates 

huuld turnish evidence erf their age, qualifications and 
>revious experience together with certificates written not 
"ore than one year prior to the date of their applications, 
rom responsible persons, testifying to their private 
haraoter. 

The Commission accepts only the age of a candidate as 
forded m the Matriculation or the Secondary School 
•inal/ heaving Certificate. In the case of a ieinale candi- 
p e whose age is not recorded in the Matriculation or 
s ^nool Final Certificate, any ol the following evidence of 
€® is accepted by the Commission: — 

b A certificate from the Headmistress of the school 
which she last attended, showing her exact age as 
recorded in the school register. 

An affidavit regarding her age sworn by her father 
or mother or some other person in a position to 
know by having been present or heard of her birth 
at the time of occurrence. 

A certificate regarding her age, from a Member of 
the Legislature or a gazetted officer, who must 
have known the candidate and her family, indicat- 
ing clearly the evidence on the basis of which he/ 
she satisfied himself /herself on the point. 

^ Candidates must enclose with their applica- 
tor ‘J 66 of He. 6 in the form of a receipted chalan 
a Government Treasury or the Reserve Bank of India 


under the head 4 ‘XXX VI — Miscellaneous — Receipts of the 
Public Service Commission, West Bengal”. Money ordero, 
cheques, etc., in lieu of treasury challans are not accepted. 
Postal order, however, may be accepted from candidates. 
They should be crossed and made payable to "The Secro- 
tary, Public Service Commission, West Bengal”. No appli- 
cation will be considered unless accompanied with the 
requisite application fee. 

Candidates abroad may deposit their application fees 
with the High Commissioner of India or the Embassy, aa 
the case may be, and obtain receipts lor the same, which 
will have to be attached to their applications to be sub- 
mitted to the Commission. 

Candidates in Government service should make sure 
bet ore depositing fee that their applications will be forward- 
ed by their superior officers. In no case will the fee paii 
with the application be refunded. 

The Commission may remit fee in case of genuine 
indigent and bona fide displaced person from Pakistan. 

An indigent displaced person shall, in the first instance, 
pay tlie application fee prescribed for a gazetted poet 
ad\ertised by the Commission but if he/she is selected for 
and apjiears at the interview, the fee paid by him/her will 
be refunded afterwards. 


Note. — “(i) A displaced person claiming age concession 
must iurnibh with his application satisfactory evidence 
that he is bona fide displaced person from Pakistan, e.g 
reiugee registration card or a certificate from a gazetted 
officer or a Member of Parliament or State Legislature, in 
original. 

(n) A member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled 
Iriho claiming age concession must furnish with his appli- 
cation a certificate in original trom a gazetted officer or a 
Member of Parliament or State Legislature belonging to 
the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, specifying the 
particular caste or tribe to which he claims to belong. 

(in) A displaced person seeking remission of the applica- 
tion lee must furnish besides the evideno© required under 
Note (i) above, a certificate (in original) from a District 
Officer or a gazetted officer or a Member of Parliament or 
State Legislature to show that he is not in a position to 
pay the prescribed fee.” 

(4) Address. — Candidates should give their present 
address and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of address. 

(5) Canvassing. — Any attempt on the part of candidates 
to enlist support of their applications through persons ol 
in II uence or officials of Government will disqualify them 
for appointment. Spontaneous recommendation from 
ixirsong interested in the candidates or otherwise known 
to them will be disregarded. 

(6) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under any Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Dnmodar Valley Corporation), in 
Fndia will ho rejected unless they are submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service. 

Candidates serving under Government or* a local or 
Statutory Body should submit an advance copy in the pros- 
cribed form. The application fee should in such cases be 
attached to the advance copy and not to the original. The 
candidature of such applicants may not however be con- 
sidered it the original applications do not reach the Com- 
mission’s office within a fortnight from the closing date. 
Unless applications in original or advance copies with 
application fees are received within the closing date, late 
applications may be rejected.

SUPPLEMENT TO THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JUNE 14, 1962

CALCUTTA IMPROVEMENT TRUST 

THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES FOR THE IMPROVE- 
MENT OF CALCUTTA 

Notice under section 43 of the Calcutta Improvement 
Act, 1911 (Bengal Act V of 1911) 

SCHEME NO. XC (PARK AT KALIGHAT ROAD) 

1. It is notified under section 43 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act, 1911, that a General Improvement 
Scheme, for the purpose of improving the area as 
regards light, air, ventilation, etc., and for the provi- 
sion of recreational facilities by providing for a Park 
in the Kalighat Road area, to be known as Scheme 
No. XC (Park at Kalighat Road) has been framed by 
the Board of Trustees for the Improvement of 
Calcutta in the above area in Ward No. 67 of the 
Corporation of Calcutta. 

2. The Boundary of the area comprised in the 
scheme, shown within red verge on plan, is as 
follows : 

On the North: Starting from the south-western 
corner of premises No. 61/1, Harish Chatter jee 
Street, running eastwards in a straight line to 
the north-western corner of premises No. 22A, 
Gobinda Ghosal Lane; from this point running 
eastwards along the northern boundary of 
premises No. 22A, Gobinda Ghosal Lane to its 
north-eastern corner. 

On the East: From this point running south 
eastwards in a straight line to the south- 
eastern corner of premises No. 43, Kalighat 
Road; from this point running southwards in 
a straight line to the south-eastern corner of 
premises Nos. 49B, 49C, 49D, Kalighat Road. 

On the South: From this point running west- 
* wards in a straight line for a distance of 128 ft. 
to a point on the southern boundary of the 
same premises situated at a distance of about 
25 ft. from the south-eastern corner of 
premises No. 53B, Kalighat Road; from this 
point running westwards along the southern 
boundary of premises Nos. 49B, 49C, 49D, 
Kalighat Road to the south-eastern corner of 
premises No. 53B, Kalighat Road; from this 
point running north-westwards in a straight 
line to the south-western corner of premises 
No. 49C, Harish Chatterjee Street. 

On the West: From this point running north 
wards in a straight line to the starting point. 

3. The particulars of the scheme, a plan showing 
the scheme area and a statement of the lands pro- 
posed for acquisition and for levy of betterment fee 
may be inspected at the office of the Trust at 10 
Netaji Subhas Road, Calcutta, between the hours 
11 a.m. and 3 p.m. on weekdays and between hours 
11 a.m. and 12-00 p.m. on Saturdays. 

Copies will be available on payment of the follow- 
ing fees : — 

Particulars and other information of the scheme 
— Re. 0.25. 

Plan of the Scheme area — Re. 1.00. 

Statement of land proposed for acquisition or for 
levy q| betterment fee — Re. 0.25. 


4. Objections to the scheme will be received up 
to the 25 th August 1962. 


5. Under section 6A of the Land Acquisition Act, 
1894, as introduced by the schedule to the Calcutta 
Improvement Act, 1911, as amended by the West 
Bengal Act XXXII of 1955; the publication of this 
notice shall have the same effect as the publication 
of notification under section 4 of the Land Acquisi- 
tion Act, 1894. 

K. SEN, 
Chairman. 

Dated, Calcutta, the 25th May 1962. 


SCHEME No. LXXXVIII (Natabar Dutta Row to 
Dharamtala Street) 

1. It is notified under section 43 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act that a Street Scheme to be known 
as Scheme No. LXXXVIII (Natabar Dutta Row to 
Dharamtala Street) for the purpose of creating new, 
or improving existing means of communication and 
facilities for traffic, remedying defective ventilation, 
providing building sites and affording better facilities 
for conservancy has been framed by the Board of 
Trustees for the Improvement of Calcutta. 

• 

2. The boundary #f the area comprised in the 
Scheme, shown within red verge on plan, is as 
follows: — 

\ 

On the North : Starting from the north-western 
corner of premises No. 36, Sasi Bhusan Dey 
Street and running eastwards along the south- 
ern edge of Ramkanai Adhikary Lane to its 
junction with Sasi Bhusan Dey Street, then in 
a straight line eastward across Sasi Bhusan 
Dev Street and Natabar Dutta Row to the 
north-western corner of premises No. 8/2A, 
Natabar Dutta Row. 

On the East: From that point running south- 
wards in a straight line along the eastern edge 
of Natabar Dutta Row for a distance of 116 ft. 
then eastwards along the northern edge of 
Natabar Dutta Row for a distance of 34 ft. 
then running towards south in a straight line 
to the south-eastern corner of premises No. 29, 
Sankharitolla Street, then southwards in a 
straight line to a point on the eastern edge 
of Ram Chandra Das Row situated at a dis- 
tance of 110 ft. from its junction with Dharam- 
tala Street measured along the eastern edge 
of the Ram Chandra Das Row. 

On the South: From that point running west- 
wards in a straight line to a point on the 
eastern edge of Indian Mirror Street situated 
at a distance of 75 ft. from its junction with 
Dharamtala Street measured along the eastern 
edge of Indian Mirror Street.

w 


On the West: From that point running north- 
wards to the north-eastern junction of Creek 
Row and Phalgun Das Lane; then running 
along the eastern edge of Phalgun Das Lane 
to the south-eastern junction of Gokul Boral 
Street and Phalgun Das Lane then in a 
straight line towards north to the north- 
western corner of premises No. 11 /ID, 
Thakurdas Palit Lane, then running north-east- 
wards in a straight line to the starting point. 

3. Further particulars of the Scheme, a plan 
showing the Scheme area and a statement of the 
lands proposed for acquisition or for levy of better- 
ment fee may be inspected at the Trust office at 
10 Nctaji Subhas Road, Calcutta, between 11 a.m. 
and 3 p.m. on weekdays and 11 a.m. and 12-30 p.m. 
on Saturday.

able on payment of the following fees : —

to 31st August 1962. 


6. Under section 6A of the Land Acquisition Act, 
1894, as introduced by the schedule to the Calcutta 
Improvement Act, 1911, as amended by the West

No. 82/152/62. Whereas the election of Shrimati 
Maya Bancrjcc as a member of the Legislative 
Assembly of the State of West Bengal from the 
Kakdwip constituency has been called in question 
by an election petition presented under Part VI of 
the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 

1951), by Shri Hrishikcsh Maity, son of Shri Bankim 
Behari Maity, Kakdwip, police-station Kakdwip, 
district 24-Parganas; 

And whereas the Election Commission has caused 
a copy of the petition to be published in the official 
gazette and has served a copy thereof by post on 
each of the respondents under sub-section (1) of 
section 86 of the Representation of the People Act, 
1951 (43 of 1951); 

Now, Therefore, in exercise of the powers con- 
ferred by sections 86 and 88 of the said Act, the 
Election Commission hereby appoints Shri Anil 
Kumar Sen, Judge, City Civil and Sessions Courts, 
Calcutta, as the member of the Election Tribunal 
for the trial of the said petition and Calcutta as the 
place where the trial of the petition shall be held.

New Delhi, the 22nd May 1962. 

NOTIFICATION 

No. 4/6/62-Poll(I). — In exercise of the powei* 
conferred by sub-section (1) read with sub-section (2) 
of section 4 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 
1961 (23 of 1961), the Central Government hereby 
declares the issue No. 16, dated the 20th April 1962 , 
of the magazine entitled “Peking Review” published 
by Peking Review Pai Wan Chuang, Peking (37), 
China, and printed in the People’s Republic of China, 
and every copy of the said issue and all other docu- 
ments containing copies, reprints and translations 
ot, or extracts from the said issue, to be forfeited to 
the Government on the ground that the article 
entitled “Sino-Indian Relations — Chinese and Indian 
Governments Exchange Notes” contained in the said 
issue, the publication of which is punishable under 
section 2 of the said Act, questions the territorial 
integrity and frontiers of India in a manner which 
is likely to be prejudicial to the interests of the 
safety and security of India.
